record.context_brief: Large splitting number with positive relation
record.original_question: Is it consistent that the splitting number s is strictly larger than ℵ2 and that the strong polarized relation \( inom{s}{\omega} 	o  inom{s}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\) still holds?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.3. Is it consistent that s > ℵ2 and (s over ω) → (s over ω)^(1,1)_2?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in ZFC. The splitting number $\mathfrak{s}$ is the least cardinality of a family $S \subseteq [\omega]^{\omega}$ such that for every $A \in [\omega]^{\omega}$ there exists $B \in S$ with both $A \cap B$ and $A \setminus B$ infinite (such a family is called a splitting family).

For cardinals $\kappa, \lambda$ and natural numbers $m,n \ge 1$, the strong polarized partition relation
$$\binom{\kappa}{\lambda} \longrightarrow \binom{\kappa}{\lambda}^{1,1}_{2}$$
asserts that for every coloring $c : \kappa \times \lambda \to 2$ there exist sets $A \subseteq \kappa$ with $|A| = \kappa$ and $B \subseteq \lambda$ with $|B| = \lambda$ such that $c \restriction (A \times B)$ is constant.

Question: Is it consistent with ZFC that simultaneously
\[ \mathfrak{s} > \aleph_{2} \quad \text{and} \quad \binom{\mathfrak{s}}{\omega} \longrightarrow \binom{\mathfrak{s}}{\omega}^{1,1}_{2}\,? \]
artifact.category_tag: Polarized partition relations and cardinal invariants
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears in work on combinatorial aspects of the splitting number and polarized partition relations. Related results show that the polarized relation $\binom{\theta}{\omega}\to\binom{\theta}{\omega}^{1,1}_2$ for all $\theta\in[\aleph_1,2^{\aleph_0}]$ is consistent, and that failure of the relation at $\mathfrak{s}$ is equivalent to existence of a strong splitting family. No source located explicitly settles the specific consistency of $\mathfrak{s} > \aleph_2$ together with the strong polarized relation at $\mathfrak{s}$, so the status remains unclear from available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Combinatorial Aspects of the Splitting Number
status_evidence.snippet: Existence of a strong splitting family is equivalent to the failure of the polarized relation (s/ω) → (s/ω)^{1,1}_2.
status_evidence.claim: Frames the question linking splitting families and the polarized relation at s.

status_evidence.title: Strong Polarized Relations for the Continuum
status_evidence.snippet: The strong polarized relation (θ/ω) → (θ/ω)^{1,1}_2 for every θ ∈ [ℵ_1, 2^{ℵ_0}] is consistent with ZFC.
status_evidence.claim: Related consistency results exist but do not specifically pin down s > ℵ_2 jointly with the relation at s.

status_evidence.title: Partition Calculus and Cardinal Invariants
status_evidence.snippet: Studies partition calculus statements involving cardinal invariants including the splitting number.
status_evidence.claim: Background reference; does not explicitly resolve the specific problem.
